{{Short description|University Professor}}
{{Orphan|date=September 2022}}

'''Alan Garfinkel''' is a professor at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] in the departments of Medicine ([[Cardiology]])<ref>{{Cite web |title=Researchers - UCLA Heart and Vascular Services |url=https://www.uclahealth.org/heart/researchers-team}}</ref> and Integrative Biology and Physiology.<ref name="hs1">{{Cite web |title=Faculty Database Production Server {{!}} David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA |url=https://people.healthsciences.ucla.edu/institution/personnel?personnel_id=46543 |access-date=2022-06-20 |website=people.healthsciences.ucla.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title= UCLA Graduate Programs in Bioscience (GPB) |url=https://bioscience.ucla.edu/people/alan-garfinkel}}</ref>
His research work applies nonlinear dynamics to cardiac [[arrhythmias]] and to the creation of biological patterns in space and time. As a teacher, he created a new course to teach dynamics and modeling to biology students, with no "calculus"  prerequisite.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Garfinkel |first1=Alan |last2=Bennoun |first2=Steve |last3=Deeds |first3=Eric |last4=Van Valkenburgh |first4=Blaire |date=2022-02-12 |title=Teaching Dynamics to Biology Undergraduates: the UCLA Experience |journal=Bulletin of Mathematical Biology |language=en |volume=84 |issue=3 |page=43 |doi=10.1007/s11538-022-00999-4 |issn=1522-9602 |pmc=8840928 |pmid=35150346}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Modeling in Biology |url=https://modelinginbiology.github.io}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Alan Garfinkel was born in Brooklyn, New York. After attending public schools in [[New York City]], he graduated from [[Cornell University]] in 1966 with a degree in Mathematics and Philosophy. After two years at [[MIT]], he moved to [[Harvard University]], where he earned a doctorate in philosophy in 1975.<ref name="hs1"/>

== Research and career ==
In Garfinkel's PhD dissertation, written under [[Hilary Putnam]], which [[Yale University Press]] published as ''Forms of Explanation'', he proposed the notion of contrastive explanation, that an answer to the question "Why X?" is really an answer to "Why X rather than a limited set of alternatives to it?"<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Miller |first=Tim |date=2021 |title=Contrastive explanation: a structural-model approach |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/knowledge-engineering-review/article/abs/contrastive-explanation-a-structuralmodel-approach/69A2E32B160C2C7FB65BC88670D7AEA7 |journal=The Knowledge Engineering Review |language=en |volume=36 |article-number=e14 |doi=10.1017/S0269888921000102 |arxiv=1811.03163 |s2cid=53209421 |issn=0269-8889}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |title=Forms of Explanation |isbn=0-300-04902-1 |last1=Garfinkel |first1=Alan |year=1981 |publisher=Yale University Press }}</ref>

He became a cardiac researcher and modeler. He and his team identified mathematical (deterministic) chaos in a real rabbit cardiac arrhythmia, then used "chaos control" techniques to stabilize the arrhythmia into periodic beating.<ref name="g 1230">{{Cite journal |last1=Garfinkel |first1=Alan |last2=Spano |first2=Mark L. |last3=Ditto |first3=William L. |last4=Weiss |first4=James N. |date=1992-08-28 |title=Controlling Cardiac Chaos |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.1519060 |journal=Science |language=en |volume=257 |issue=5074 |pages=1230–1235 |doi=10.1126/science.1519060 |pmid=1519060 |bibcode=1992Sci...257.1230G |s2cid=30011623 |issn=0036-8075|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Using analytical techniques from nonlinear dynamics, he and his colleagues Zhilin Qu and James N. Weiss then demonstrated that [[ventricular fibrillation]] (VF), the primary cause of sudden cardiac death, is an example of deterministic spatiotemporal chaos, and devised and experimentally verified a mechanism to prevent VF.<ref name="prevent">{{Cite journal |last1=Garfinkel |first1=Alan |last2=Kim |first2=Young-Hoon |last3=Voroshilovsky |first3=Olga |last4=Qu |first4=Zhilin |last5=Kil |first5=Jong R. |last6=Lee |first6=Moon-Hyoung |last7=Karagueuzian |first7=Hrayr S. |last8=Weiss |first8=James N. |last9=Chen |first9=Peng-Sheng |date=2000-05-23 |title=Preventing ventricular fibrillation by flattening cardiac restitution |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |language=en |volume=97 |issue=11 |pages=6061–6066 |doi=10.1073/pnas.090492697 |issn=0027-8424 |pmc=18558 |pmid=10811880|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Garfinkel |first1=Alan |last2=Weiss |first2=James N. |last3=Baher |first3=Ali |last4=Yang |first4=Junzhong |last5=Qu |first5=Zhilin |last6=Xie |first6=Fagen |date=2004-03-10 |title=A simulation study of the effects of cardiac anatomy in ventricular fibrillation |journal=The Journal of Clinical Investigation |language=en |volume=113 |issue=5 |pages=686–693 |doi=10.1172/JCI17341 |issn=1558-8238 |pmc=351312 |pmid=14991066}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Krishnamoorthi |first1=Shankarjee |last2=Perotti |first2=Luigi E. |last3=Borgstrom |first3=Nils P. |last4=Ajijola |first4=Olujimi A. |last5=Frid |first5=Anna |last6=Ponnaluri |first6=Aditya V. |last7=Weiss |first7=James N. |last8=Qu |first8=Zhilin |last9=Klug |first9=William S. |last10=Ennis |first10=Daniel B. |last11=Garfinkel |first11=Alan |date=2014-12-10 |title=Simulation Methods and Validation Criteria for Modeling Cardiac Ventricular Electrophysiology |journal=PLOS ONE |language=en |volume=9 |issue=12 |article-number=e114494 |doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0114494 |issn=1932-6203 |pmc=4262432 |pmid=25493967|bibcode=2014PLoSO...9k4494K |doi-access=free }}</ref>

His research interests include the electrophysiology of cells and tissues modeled mathematically, analysis of experimental and clinical arrhythmia data with techniques of nonlinear dynamics, and research and development of pharmacologic and electrophysiological therapies to prevent or regulate arrhythmias. He also studies the role of physiological and pathophysiological oscillations in biological systems, with a particular focus on the mechanisms of their creation and destruction,<ref>{{Cite journal He started his career as a professor of the [[philosophy of science]] at [[California State University, Northridge]]. Moving to the University of California, Los Angeles, he held  a succession of positions leading to Professor of Medicine (Cardiology) and Integrative Biology and Physiology (2003–2018), where he is currently Research Professor  and Professor Emeritus. In 2019–2020, he was Newton Abraham Visiting {{not a typo|Professor}} in the Department of Computer Science and Lincoln College, [[University of Oxford]].<ref>{{Cite web |title= Newton Abraham Lecture | website=[[YouTube]] |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XhJkFPHi4ak}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Garfinkel has received awards including Astor Visiting Lecturer, University of Oxford, UCLA University Distinguished Teaching Award (2015) and many others. His text ''Modeling Life'' was awarded the Textbook Excellence Award of the Textbook and Academic Authors Association.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Past Textbook Award Recipients |url=https://www.taaonline.net/past-textbook-award-recipients |access-date=2022-06-20 |website=www.taaonline.net}}</ref> His patents include "Real time stabilizing system for pulsating activity" (US5447520A).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Six faculty selected for UCLA Academic Senate Distinguished Teaching Award |url=https://newsroom.ucla.edu/dept/faculty/five-faculty-selected-for-ucla-academic-senate-distinguished-teaching-awards |access-date=2022-06-20 |website=UCLA |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=wp-misc.lifesci.ucla.edu |url=https://wp-misc.lifesci.ucla.edu/divisional/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2018/06/LS-Excellence-Awards.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{Cite patent|number=5447520|title=Real time stabilizing system for pulsating activity|country=US|pubdate=1995-09-05|assign1=[[The Regents of the University of California]]|inventor1-last=Spano|inventor1-first=Mark L.|inventor2-last=Ditto|inventor2-first=William L.|inventor3-last=Garfinkel|inventor3-first=Alan|inventor4-last=Weiss|inventor4-first=James N.}}</ref>
